about: Nothing To Do Here shows a round-headed rage comic character with a blank, completely unbothered expression, strapped into a jet pack and calmly flying off to the side in a puff of smoke. He doesn't panic or argue; he just leaves. The image is the internet's way of quietly exiting a situation that has become awkward, toxic, too complicated or simply not your problem, with the deadpan face doing all the talking.
origin: Jet Pack Guy was drawn in 2011 on Cuanto Cabrón, a Spanish rage comic site, and the drawing traveled to English-speaking image boards as a reply for threads people wanted to leave.
usage:
The top box sets up the situation you want to escape: an argument in the comments, a family dinner topic, a production outage, a messy group chat. The bottom box is usually "nothing to do here" or a similar line about leaving.

Use it as a comment reply or to show yourself backing away from something. The joke is the calm exit, so keep the bottom line flat and short rather than dramatic.
ideas: when the family dinner turns to politics
when the group chat starts planning a trip
when someone asks who broke the build
when the teacher asks for volunteers
